cards.front: Recall a key point about Tenses: Present, Preterite and Imperfect
cards.back: This topic covers key vocabulary and structures for tenses: present, preterite and imperfect. You need to know the topic vocabulary, be able to use it in all four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), and express opinions with reasons.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse spanish exam tips?
cards.back: Use present tense for facts, habits and descriptions. Use preterite for completed actions in the past. Use imperfect for ongoing or habitual past actions, descriptions and background. Know the key trigger words for each tense.
the present tense (e.g. Uso el presente para rutinas)

cards.front: What does el pretérito indefinido mean?
cards.back: the preterite tense (e.g. El pretérito expresa acciones completadas)
the imperfect tense (e.g. El imperfecto describe el pasado)
the stem/root (e.g. La raíz del verbo 'hablar' es 'habl-')
the ending (e.g. Las terminaciones cambian según el tiempo)

cards.front: What does el verbo irregular mean?
cards.back: the irregular verb (e.g. Ser y ir son verbos irregulares)
to conjugate (e.g. Hay que conjugar los verbos correctamente)

cards.front: What does el marcador temporal mean?
cards.back: the time marker (e.g. 'Ayer' es un marcador temporal del pretérito)

cards.front: What does el cambio vocálico mean?
cards.back: the vowel change (e.g. Pienso tiene un cambio vocálico e→ie)

cards.front: What does la acción completada mean?
cards.back: the completed action (e.g. El pretérito indica una acción completada)

cards.front: What does la acción habitual mean?
cards.back: the habitual action (e.g. El imperfecto describe acciones habituales)
the routine (e.g. Mi rutina diaria incluye estudiar español)
Writing task: Write about present tense, preterite tense, imperfect tense, regular and irregular verbs, when to use each tense.
